title: The derived category of a braided abelian monoidal category is braided
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensor product is additive in each variable, and with a braiding: a natural isomorphism $\beta_{X,Y}\colon X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$ satisfying the two hexagon identities $\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(\beta_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z)$ and $\alpha^{-1}_{Z,X,Y}\circ\beta_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,Y,Z}=(\beta_{X,Z}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Y)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,Z,Y}\circ(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes\beta_{Y,Z})$. Assume the graded tensor products and their compatibility with reassociation exist so that the direct-sum total tensor makes the category of $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complexes and its homotopy category $K(C)$ monoidal. Let $D(C)$ and $Q_h\colon K(C)\to D(C)$ be the derived category and its localization functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume $Q_h$ carries the derived monoidal structure: $D(C)$ has a functor $\otimes^L\colon D(C)\times D(C)\to D(C)$ with a natural transformation $\mu_{X,Y}\colon Q_hX\otimes^LQ_hY\to Q_h(X\otimes Y)$ that is a binary left derived functor of the tensor on $K(C)$, meaning that for every functor $V\colon D(C)\times D(C)\to D(C)$ composition with $\mu$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(V,\otimes^L)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ(Q_h\times Q_h),Q_h\circ\otimes)$; the two parenthesized triple tensors and the right-parenthesized fourfold tensor, with their composite comparison maps built from $\mu$, have the corresponding three- and four-variable universal properties, and tensoring on either side with $Q_h\mathbf 1$, with the comparison maps $\mu_{\mathbf 1,-}$ and $\mu_{-,\mathbf 1}$, has the corresponding one-variable universal properties. The associator and unitors on $D(C)$ are those induced by these universal properties. Then $D(C)$ is braided monoidal for this derived tensor product, in the sense above, with braiding obtained from the Koszul braiding of $K(C)$ by the binary left derived universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-homotopy-category-koszul-braided] with cochain shape $\mathrm{up}(\mathbf Z)$. Its tensor-existence hypotheses are among the assumed graded tensor and reassociation hypotheses. It gives a natural braiding $\beta^K_{X,Y}\colon X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$ on $K(C)$, induced on the homogeneous summand of degrees $(p,q)$ by $(-1)^{pq}\beta_{X^p,Y^q}$, satisfying both hexagons. Thus the source category to be localized is braided; no assertion that tensor preserves all quasi-isomorphisms has been made.

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $D(C)$ is the localization of $K(C)$ at the images $W$ of quasi-isomorphisms. These contain identities: an identity induces the identity on every cohomology object. Set $L=Q_h$. The assumed derived tensor and its canonical associator and unitors give precisely the derived monoidal structure for this localization. In particular the triple universal properties needed for hexagons are hypotheses, rather than being inferred from the binary property alone.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-derived-monoidal-braided-transport] to the braided category $K(C)$, the class $W$, and $L=Q_h$. All its hypotheses were checked above. Its output is a braiding on the given derived tensor of $D(C)$ and includes both hexagon identities. More explicitly, if $\mu_{X,Y}\colon LX\otimes^L LY\to L(X\otimes Y)$ is the comparison, its lifted braiding $b$ satisfies $\mu_{Y,X}\circ b_{LX,LY}=L(\beta^K_{X,Y})\circ\mu_{X,Y}$, and its inverse is the corresponding lift of $(\beta^K)^{-1}$. The cited transport theorem gives mutually inverse natural transformations, so these are isomorphisms. Since $\beta^K$ is the Koszul braiding identified in step 1, this is exactly the required braiding induced by the binary left derived universal property.
